analysis:
Reviewed all three primary analyses against the replayed patches, file metadata and changelog source. .github/workflows/provider-plan.yml:183-185 removes the size-required marker from the two product-build lanes and cluster-release-checks. This expands Sandbox routing when job shapes are disabled; it does not remove a required test/result gate. Job predicates, explicit sizes and fallback labels remain unchanged in these hunks. .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml:56-58,862-864 changes only comments. docs/developer/build.md:589-600,623-628 and changelog.d/ci-build-lanes-routed.md:3-5 consistently describe approval-pinned sizing and 12 requested macOS jobs.
No supplied evidence establishes an authorization bypass, skipped security check, unsafe runner, artifact tampering or release-qualification bypass. Smaller approved runners present a documented build-performance risk, not a demonstrated security regression. GitHub build caches are distinct from the encrypted inference prefix cache in T-041; no supplied change touches runtime encryption, attestation, billing, privileged helpers or inference admission.
The local questions remain unresolved: the routing/approval implementation and build-product/cache actions are not supplied in the replay. Further review should verify approval enforcement, fallback and lane-cap behavior, plus runner isolation and artifact/cache integrity for newly routed product producers. These contracts matter to A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054, but missing implementations are not evidence of missing controls, nor is there evidence that these test products become qualified release artifacts. Replay is explicitly incomplete (8 source units omitted), so surrounding workflow controls described by prior analyses could not all be independently verified. No supported finding; runner and product-trust uncertainty remains material to the routing expansion.
